answer_1.quote: We propose an LLM-based rewriting approach to inappropriateness mitigation... The policy π_RL is optimized using PPO to generate an improved version ŷ from the input argument x while preserving the content of x as much as possible and making the argument more appropriate.
answer_1.outputs: rewritten arguments that are more appropriate while preserving semantic content

answer_2.quote: We automatically evaluate the generated rewrites using the five appropriateness classifiers... We calculate the following performance values: App., Sim. (BERTScore), NES (Normalized Edit Similarity), PPL (perplexity), GM (geometric mean of App., Sim., and 1/PPL).

answer_4.quote: We hired native English speakers on Upwork.com to evaluate the rewrites... In the first study, the annotators scored each rewrite regarding three quality metrics: Appropriateness, Meaning preservation (Similarity), and Fluency using a 5-point Likert scale.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to rate each rewrite on appropriateness, similarity to the original argument, and fluency on a 5‑point Likert scale.
